data: Fictitious fixtures only; no public geocoding service or live provider was used.

checks.evidence: The controlled fetch double returned a fictitious label and valid finite coordinates; the selector preserved label and coordinates.
Incomplete JSON, wrong field types, NaN and out-of-range coordinates were rejected; manual output contained no coordinates.
An abort-aware controlled fetch double reproduced the timeout and produced an unavailable result.
A controlled HTTP 429 response produced rate_limited and was not cached.
A controlled fetch rejection reproduced a network disconnection and produced an unavailable result.
The UI integration test submitted the exact user-entered fictitious building reference, including surrounding spaces, after timeout.
A valid normalized query reused a cache entry, TTL expiry caused a fresh fetch, and invalid/429 responses were not cached.
The local controlled backend self-test passed its fictitious geocoding success, rate-limit, server-error, incomplete, invalid-coordinate and malformed-response scenarios.
